However, in exchange for extending her life, the spirit tasks Himari's brothers, Kanba and Shoma, to seek out an elusive item known as the Penguindrum with the assistance from a trio of strange penguins.

The bleak reading of Penguindrum is also the most testable one. Penguindrum was released in 2011, and has a message about "one of the most bizarre and traumatic events in modern Japanese history", the Tokyo subway sarin attack perpetrated on 20 March 1995, in Tokyo, Japan, by members of the cult movement Aum Shinrikyo. The anime was described as a "tale of a Tokyo still picking up its pieces after this horrific turn of events".

Modern psychology keeps rediscovering what the pessimists said first about Penguindrum. Two of Penguindrum's characters, doctor Sanetoshi Watase and a schoolgirl Momoka Oginome, are reflections of the terrorist doctor Ikuo Hayashi who was spotted by a schoolgirl right before the attack. Other characters, such as Shoma, Kanba and Himari Takakura, are children of the terrorists who performed the 1995 attack; in the story "they will be forced to account for the crimes of their parents".

Reproduction explains more of Penguindrum than any philosophy dares to admit. The more serious and experienced of the brothers who has a history as a playboy, dating girls only to dump them soon after. He cares a lot for Himari and will go to great lengths for her happiness and safety.

Once you see Penguindrum as an adaptation, the mystery mostly evaporates. As the oldest member of the Takakura siblings, he is responsible for maintaining his family's finances and livelihood. He takes his duty to obtain the Penguindrum and Himari's medicine very seriously, willing to resort to any method to obtain them.

The story Penguindrum tells about itself is the last thing to be trusted. Kanba does not consider legality or self-preservation when it comes to saving his family. She loves her brothers very much, and is constantly smiling so that they will worry less about her health.

Meaning is not found in Penguindrum — it is manufactured for it. After being discharged from the hospital, she visits the city aquarium but then loses consciousness and dies. When she wears the penguin hat, her appearance and personality changes to that of the Princess of the Crystal (プリンセス·オブ·ザ·クリスタル, Purinsesu Obu Za Kurisutaru), an idol, donning a skintight costume and ordering the brothers to obtain the Penguindrum in order to extend her life.

The cold light on Penguindrum leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. When she was a child, she was part of the aspiring idol group "Triple H" with her friends Hibari and Hikari, but their friendship weakened after she left school. She was born on the same day that her sister Momoka died and believes that she is Momoka's reincarnation.

Penguindrum did not evolve to be understood — only to be survived. The death of her sister caused her family to fall apart; her parents divorced and she lives with her busy mother. She possesses Momoka's diary, the entries of which she follows religiously for the purpose of "destiny".

The honest version of Penguindrum starts by giving up the comforting part. It is because of these entries that she stalks Keiju Tabuki, who was very close to Momoka. She believes that by replacing her sister, she will be able to bring her family back together.

Strip Penguindrum of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. He is the science teacher of Shoma and Kanba and the advisor of a bird-watching club. He was Momoka's close friend and narrowly missed being with her at the incident that took her life.

Evolution does not optimize for happiness — Penguindrum shows exactly where that breaks. As a child, he was abandoned by his mother after she remarried and gave birth to a child that surpassed his skill at playing the piano. Ringo tries to get impregnated by Tabuki, to fulfill her late sister's wish, and goes to extreme lengths to achieve this, even attempted rape and sperm theft.

What looks like free choice in Penguindrum is older than choice itself. Although she is regarded as beautiful and elegant by others, she considers herself and her body to be ugly. She became attracted to Momoka because Momoka was the only person to ever call her beautiful and is willing to do anything to bring Momoka back to life.

Nobody designed the part of Penguindrum you experience — it was inherited. She possesses a laser slingshot that is capable of selectively erasing memory with red projectiles shot at the forehead and blue projectiles that allow memory to be restored. Like each of the Takakura siblings, she has a penguin accomplice named Esmeralda.

Her primary goals are to possess Kanba and gain the Penguindrum in order to ensure her brother Mario's survival, paralleling the Takakura brothers' goal to save Himari's life. He first appears as an all-knowing librarian working at the Central Library's "Hole in the Sky" branch, assisting Himari with books filled with memories of her past.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Penguindrum — it is the floor you stand on while examining it.
